ai.description: This lizard reaches a snout-vent length of 7 cm. It is bronze-brown dorsally with a distinct pale dorsolateral stripe and a dark lateral band. Key features include a smooth body and keeled scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Eutropis nagarjunensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a single pair of enlarged nuchal scales, which are absent in most other similar Indian *Eutropis* species.
ai.habitat: *Eutropis nagarjunensis* is endemic to the rocky, scrub-covered hills of the Eastern Ghats in Andhra Pradesh, typically found at elevations between 300 and 600 meters.
ai.behavior: Eutropis nagarjunensis is a diurnal skink that actively hunts for small insects among rocky crevices and leaf litter during the warmest hours of the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Eutropis nagarjunensis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 3 to 5 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Eutropis nagarjunensis* is endemic to the Eastern Ghats of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, primarily found in rocky, scrub-forest habitats at low to moderate elevations.
